name: Idaho
overview: Idaho offers income-tested Property Tax Reduction (PTR), a separate disabled-veteran benefit, and state-funded homeowner property-tax bill credits.

programs.name: Property Tax Reduction (Circuit Breaker)
programs.ageRule: Age 65+ or qualifying widowhood, disability, blindness, former POW/hostage status, or orphaned child.
programs.incomeDefinition: Prior-calendar-year total income after qualifying medical expenses.
programs.incomeLimits: 2025 property-tax program uses 2024 income of $37,810 or less.
programs.maximumBenefit: 2025 income schedule ranges from $250 to $1,500, limited by qualifying taxes.
programs.formulaSummary: Income-table reduction applied to home and up to one acre.
eligibilityNotes: Applicants must use the Idaho property as their primary residence and qualify for the homeowner exemption.

Applicants whose current-year home assessment exceeds the greater of $400,000 or 200% of their county's median assessment for homes with the homeowner exemption are referred to the property-tax deferral program instead.
This value limit does not apply to veterans with a VA-certified 100% service-connected disability rating, or an individual-unemployability rating compensated at the 100% rate.
interactions: Other homeowner relief affects remaining taxes; avoid double counting.

sources.title: Idaho Code §63-705, income schedule and home-value limit

programs.name: Disabled Veterans Property Tax Reduction
programs.ageRule: Qualifying 100% service-connected disability or VA individual-unemployability compensation.
programs.formulaSummary: Fixed maximum tax reduction on qualifying home and up to one acre.
programs.application: Apply to assessor by April 15, 2025; permanent-and-total rules affect reapplication.
eligibilityNotes: Primary residence and homeowner exemption required.
Qualifying surviving spouse may continue on the same property.

programs.name: Homeowner and Additional Property Tax Relief
programs.maximumBenefit: Variable state-funded bill credit, limited to applicable taxes.
programs.formulaSummary: State allocations reduce eligible property-tax bills; calculation depends on levy/property and funding inputs.
programs.application: County administration for qualifying properties; verify the bill's relief line items.
eligibilityNotes: Homeowner exemption and program certification rules apply.
This program uses separate rules from the income-tested PTR schedule.
interactions: Apply relief in statutory order; underlying taxes and other credits cannot be double counted.

sources.title: Homeowner and additional property-tax relief, December 2025

programs.name: Real estate taxes in Idaho itemized deductions
programs.ageRule: No age test on this deduction.
programs.incomeDefinition: Idaho starts with federal itemized deductions. Federal modified adjusted gross income can reduce the combined federal deduction for state and local taxes.
programs.incomeLimits: Idaho imposes no separate income limit on this component. The federal combined limit can fall for single filers with federal modified adjusted gross income above $500,000 in 2025.
programs.maximumBenefit: Qualified real estate taxes within the federal combined state and local tax limit. The deduction reduces taxable income.
programs.formulaSummary: Idaho subtracts the Schedule A deduction for state and local income or general sales taxes and retains eligible real estate taxes within the federal limit.
programs.application: Use federal Schedule A to complete Idaho Form 40 lines 13 through 15. Compare the result with the standard deduction on line 16.
eligibilityNotes: Use the federal qualified real estate tax amount on Schedule A line 5b.
interactions: Idaho applies the larger of the state itemized deduction and standard deduction. Federal Schedule A and the federal combined state and local tax limit determine the starting amount.
programs.programYear: 2025 Idaho income-tax return, based on the 2025 federal Schedule A.

sources.title: 2025 Idaho Form 40 instructions for itemized deductions

researchNotes: The 2025 PTR income limit is not the 2026 limit based on 2025 income.
Homeowner bill credits depend on county and tax-code-area inputs; the report provides no statewide flat payment.
Idaho also offers a homeowner assessed-value exemption and property-tax deferral.
The published 2025 PTR income table contains overlapping and omitted interior ranges. The report provides no calculator that assigns awards at those boundaries or resolves income rounding.
The December 2025 homeowner-relief report lists county semiannual FY2026 transfers rather than parcel awards. Parcel calculations require certified rolls, eligible levies and county allocations.

sources.title: Homeowner and additional property-tax relief, December 2025
